subject.title: Feature Request: tools.cron.tools.deny config option for cron job tool restrictions

question: Should isolated cron jobs get a first-class tools.cron.tools.allow/deny policy, inherit tools.subagents.tools, or continue with only per-job payload.toolsAllow plus delivery safeguards?
rationale: This choice defines a scheduled-run tool-access boundary and public config contract, including whether existing announce-mode cron jobs that directly use message keep working by default.

options.title: Add Cron-Scoped Policy
options.body: Introduce tools.cron.tools.allow/deny with explicit precedence and tests for message-tool denial across cron delivery modes.

options.title: Inherit Subagent Policy
options.body: Apply tools.subagents.tools to cron sessions too, reducing config surface while coupling two different execution modes.

options.title: Keep Per-Job Only
options.body: Avoid a new global cron policy and rely on payload.toolsAllow, docs, and delivery safeguards for scheduled runs.

recommendation.title: Add Cron-Scoped Policy
recommendation.body: Introduce tools.cron.tools.allow/deny with explicit precedence and tests for message-tool denial across cron delivery modes.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined signal from cron tool-policy review context, runner history, and current policy/config surfaces.
